'''Rolf Landsberg''' ({{birth date|1920|2|28}} – {{birth date|2003|12|27}}) was a German [[Professor]] of [[Physical Chemistry]].<ref name=HumbobitRL/>

Between 1961/2 and 1964 he served as rector of the [[:de:Technische Hochschule Leuna-Merseburg|Leuna-Merseburg "Carl Schorlemmer" Academy for Chemistry]] (near [[Leipzig]]).<ref name=LeibnizSozRL>{{cite web|url=http://leibnizsozietaet.de/wp-content/uploads/2012/11/03_nekrologe.pdf|title=Nachrufe für verstorbene Mitglieder und Freunde der Leibniz-Sozietät: Rolf Landsberg *28.2.1920 † 27.12.2003 |work=Sitzungsberichte der Leibniz-Sozietät |volume= 74 |issue= 2004|page=35|author1=Lothar Müller|author2=Heinz Kautzleben|publisher=Leibniz-Sozietät der Wissenschaften zu Berlin e.V., Berlin|date=|accessdate=21 March 2015}}</ref><ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL>{{cite web |url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=2001 |author2=Dieter Hoffmann |author1= [[Bernd-Rainer Barth]]|title=Landsberg, Rolf *28.2.1920, † 27.12.2003 Chemiker, Rektor der Technischen Hochschule für Chemie Leuna-Merseburg |publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |language= German| accessdate= 21 March 2015}}</ref>

==Life==
Rolf Landsberg was the elder of two sons born to the architect [[:de:Max Landsberg (Architekt)|Max Landsberg]] and his wife, the doctor Hedwig Landsberg.  Theirs was a prosperous [[Berlin]] family. However, Max Landsberg, who had been diagnosed with epilepsy in 1890, died young, in 1930.<ref name=MyraWarMaLa>{{cite journal|url=http://www.juedische-architekten.de/publik/pub1d.htm|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20030807234221/http://www.juedische-architekten.de/publik/pub1d.htm|url-status=dead|archive-date=2003-08-07|title=Max Landsberg, Berlin 1878 - Berlin 1930|journal=Mitteilungen, Berlin|author=Myra Warhaftig|volume=4/1992|pages=18–23}}</ref>   Rolf began his schooling in Berlin, starting his secondary education at the Heinrich-Kleist-Gymnasium. However, in January 1933 there had been a [[Machtergreifung|change of government]], and it became increasingly apparent that [[antisemitism]], which had been a prominent feature of Nazi rhetoric in opposition, was entering the political mainstream. The Landsbergs were [[Jewish]]. In 1934 Rolf Landsberg was sent to school in England, where he attended the progressive [[St Christopher School]] in [[Letchworth]], to the north of [[London]] between 1934 and 1937. Sources differ as to whether his mother and brother accompanied him to England at this stage, but by 1939 all three had emigrated to [[United Kingdom|Britain]].<ref name=LeibnizSozRL/>   He went on to study at [[University College London]], emerging with a Chemistry degree (Bachelor of Science) in 1940.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL/>   In Britain he later also studied at [[Aberystwyth University|Aberystwyth]], but his academic progress was not uninterrupted.<ref name=LeibnizSozRL/>

In 1939 [[Germany]] invaded [[Poland]] and [[United Kingdom|Britain]] declared war on Germany. At home the British government responded to these developments by identifying as [[Enemy alien#United Kingdom|enemy aliens]] large numbers of Jewish and political refugees who had arrived from [[Nazi Germany]]. Landsberg's mother was able to escape to Brazil where she joined her brother who, in 1936, had also fled Germany.<ref name=CenJewHisHH>{{cite web |title=Die Familie und das Leben des Hans Hamburger, 1854-1953: Memoirs and biographies|url=http://access.cjh.org/query.php?term=Hans+Hamburger&qtype=basic&stype=contains&paging=25&dtype=any&repo=all&go=#1|author=Hamburger, Charlotte|publisher=Center for Jewish History, New York|accessdate=21 March 2015}}</ref>   Rolf and his brother were both arrested by the British government in 1940, and while his younger brother 
was interned on the [[Isle of Man]], Rolf was sent to [[Canada]] for his internment. In Canada he became associated with the (exiled) [[Communist Party of Germany|German Communist Party]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL/>   Two years later the political mood had changed and he was returned to Britain where he played an active part in the struggle against [[Fascism]] in Europe,<ref name=HumbobitRL>{{cite web|url=http://www2.hu-berlin.de/presse/zeitung/archiv/03_04/num_4/aktuell.pdf
|title=Personalia .... Prof. Dr. Rolf Landsberg starb am 27. Dezember 2003 im Alter von 83 Jahren. Er wurde ...|publisher=Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin |page=2 |date=22 January 2004 |accessdate=21 March 2015}}</ref> and became a co-founder of an exiled London based version of the anti-Nazi [[Free German Youth|Free German Youth (FDJ / ''Freie Deutsche Jugend'')]] movement.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL/>   In 1944 he volunteered as an assistant to the British army, with which he worked for the next three years, notably as a simultaneous translator, until September 1947. Postings included [[Münster]] and [[Bielefeld]].

Towards the end of 1947 Rolf Landsberg relocated full-time to Germany where he obtained a post as an assistant in the [[Physical Chemistry]] Institute at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]], which was in the [[Soviet occupation zone]] of what remained of Germany. The division of Berlin seemed at this stage neither so politically absolute nor so physically rigid as it later became, but the basis for a return to [[One-party state|one-]][[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|party]] government had already been set in place in April 1946 with the [[Merger of the KPD and SPD into the Socialist Unity Party of Germany|contentious merger]] between the old [[Communist Party of Germany|Communist Party]] and the Moderate-left [[Social Democratic Party of Germany|SPD]]. Landsberg joined the newly formed [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|Socialist Unity Party]] (''Sozialistische Einheitspartei Deutschlands'', SED) in 1947,<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL/> and by 1949, when the [[Soviet Military Administration in Germany|Soviet controlled]] part of Germany was re-founded as the [[German Democratic Republic]], [[Group of Soviet Forces in Germany|sponsored by]] and in many respects politically modeled on the [[Soviet Union]], Landsberg was a citizen of the new country, while his younger brother [[:de:Peter Landsberg|Peter]] pursued an academic career in England.<ref name=PetLanobit>{{cite web| url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/7741783/Professor-Peter-Landsberg.html |title=Professor Peter Landsberg: Professor Peter Landsberg, who died on February 14 aged 87, was a theoretical physicist of outstanding breadth; his areas of particular expertise were ...|publisher=[[Daily Telegraph]] (online), London|author=[[Peter Dunn (engineer)|Peter Dunn]]|date=19 May 2010|accessdate=21 March 2015|display-authors=etal}}</ref>

After three years, in 1950, Ralf Landsberg received his doctorate from the Humboldt for a dissertation supervised by [[Karl Friedrich Bonhoeffer]] and entitled "Potentials in the creation of precipitate membranes"<ref>''"Potentiale bei der Bildung von Niederschlagsmembranen"''</ref><ref name=RoLaPromDiss>{{cite web|url=http://www.genealogy-theochem.de/view.php?id=1352
|title=Rolf Landsberg|publisher=Theoretische Chemie, Leibniz Universität Hannover|author=Prof. Dr. Karl Jug (webpage contact)
|work=Theoretical Chemistry Genealogy Project|accessdate=21 March 2015}}</ref>   The next step in his career involved a move, in 1952, to the [[University of Greifswald|Ernst Moritz Arndt University (Greifswald)]], in the north-east of the country, where he lectured on [[physical chemistry]].<ref name=LeibnizSozRL/>   This was followed by a longer stint, starting in 1955, in the south, as a lecturer at the [[:de:Technische Hochschule Leuna-Merseburg|Leuna-Merseburg "Carl Schorlemmer" Academy for Chemistry]].<ref name=LeibnizSozRL/>  It was at Leuna-Merseburg that he received his [[Habilitation]] (a higher academic distinction) in 1958/59.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL/><ref name=RoLaHabiDiss/>   On this occasion his dissertation was entitled "On the kinetics of concealed processes with nickel and zinc anodes"<ref name=RoLaHabiDiss>{{cite web|url=http://www.genealogy-theochem.de/vita.php?id=1352&lng=de|title=Rolf Landsberg| publisher=Theoretische Chemie, Leibniz Universität Hannover|author=Prof. Dr. Karl Jug (webpage contact)|work=Theoretical Chemistry Genealogy Project|accessdate=21 March 2015}}</ref><ref>''"Zur Kinetik der Bedeckungsvorgänge an Nickel- und Zinkanoden"''</ref>   In 1959 he became a professor at the same institution.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL/>   Then, in January 1962, Rolf Landsberg was appointed Rector of the [[:de:Technische Hochschule Leuna-Merseburg|Leuna-Merseburg "Carl Schorlemmer" Academy for Chemistry]]<ref name=LeibnizSozRL/> in succession to [[:de:Elmar Profft|Elmar Profft]]. Profft himself had been released from the post after less than a year after making known political and ideological differences with [[Socialist Unity Party of Germany|The Party]] over matters including, notably, the [[Berlin Wall]] erected suddenly in August 1961.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenEP>{{cite web |url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=2728 |author1=Dieter Hoffmann |title=Profft, Elmar *28.5.1905, † 12.1.1978 Chemiker, Rektor der Technischen Hochschule für Chemie »Carl Schorlemmer« Leuna-Merseburg|publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |language= German| accessdate= 21 March 2015}}</ref>

Just two years later, in 1964, he returned to the [[Humboldt University of Berlin]], accepting the chair for [[Physical Chemistry]], also becoming Director of the Humboldt's Physical Chemistry Institute. His predecessor's academic career (followed a few months later by his party membership) had been abruptly terminated following a series of lectures in 1963/64 which had been interpreted as a call to remove political dogma from science teaching.<ref name=JenaRH>{{cite web| url=http://www.jena.de/de/232606|title=Havemann - Dialektik ohne Dogma |author=Dr. Rüdiger Stutz |publisher=Stadtverwaltung Jena|date=|accessdate=21 March 2015}}</ref>   In this instance Landsberg's dissident predecessor was [[Robert Havemann]] who subsequently gained prominence in various sources on account of the persecution he suffered at the hands of the [[East Germany|East German]] authorities.<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRH>{{cite web |url=http://bundesstiftung-aufarbeitung.de/wer-war-wer-in-der-ddr-%2363%3B-1424.html?ID=1272 |author1=Dieter Hoffmann |title=Havemann, Robert *11.3.1910, † 9.4.1982 Physikochemiker, Dissident|publisher= Bundesstiftung zur Aufarbeitung der SED-Diktatur: Biographische Datenbanken |language= German| accessdate= 21 March 2015}}</ref>

A particular focus of Landsberg's career in terms of research involved surfaces.  That is what he now concentrated on at the [[Humboldt University of Berlin|Humboldt]] [[physical chemistry|Physical Chemistry Institute]] until his retirement in 1985.<ref name=LeibnizSozRL/>  His many years of teaching in the field of electro-chemistry were crystallised in the book "Electro-chemical Reactions and Processes" (1977).<ref name=LeibnizSozRL/><ref>''"Elektrochemische Reaktionen und Prozesse"''</ref>

He continued to play an active role in scientific life after his retirement, and was a board member of the [[:de:Leibniz-Sozietät|Leibniz Society]] in Berlin which he had joined in 1993.<ref name=HumbobitRL/>   He was also a member of the [[German Academy of Sciences at Berlin|German Academy of Sciences]].<ref name=BiographischeDatenbankenRL/>
